The Looks

Choose Your Transformation

Look 01

The Pixie

Effortless. Editorial. Unbothered.

Short, textured, done in five minutes. The pixie is the power move that says you don't need hair to command a room — your face does the work.

Maintenance
Salon tripsEvery 4–6 weeks for shape
Best forStage, TV, keynotes
Black women who own this Lupita Nyong'o, Toni Braxton, Halle Berry
On you: Your high cheekbones and bright eyes would eat this up. The shorter the hair, the more the face shows — and yours is the one you want people to see.

Look 02

The Big Chop

Fearless. Powerful. Pure.

The most radical softness. A shaved or close-cropped head is one of the boldest statements a woman can make — and on the right face, it is pure art.

Maintenance
Salon tripsMonthly trim or DIY
Best forEvery occasion — it never clashes
Black women who own this Danai Gurira, Amber Rose, early Erykah Badu
On you: This is the "I woke up and chose power" look. Your bone structure is built for it. Big hoops and this cut would make every room stop cold.

Look 03

The Farrah — Black Edition

Retro Glam. Runway. Showstopper.

Voluminous feathered wings that frame the face — but make it Black girl magic. Think Chaka Khan meets Studio 54, straight into your next keynote or red carpet.

Maintenance
Achievable viaBlowout + flat iron, wig, or weave
Best forMedia appearances, speaking, events
Black women who own this Chaka Khan, SZA, '70s Diana Ross
On you: This is your TLC / Jennifer Hudson Show hair. It photographs beautifully and adds serious presence on stage or screen. The volume frames a round face perfectly.

Look 04

Knotless Box Braids

Protective. Versatile. Iconic.

The look that does everything. Up for a board meeting, down for brunch, half-up for a keynote. Low-manipulation protective styling that looks intentional at every length.

Maintenance
Duration6–8 weeks, touch up edges
Best forTravel, busy seasons, content creation
Black women who own this Beyoncé, Zendaya, Janet Jackson (Poetic Justice era)
On you: Knotless mid-back braids with gold beads at the ends would be stunning for content — they move beautifully on camera and match your whole brand energy.

Look 05

Sisterlocks / Locs

Rooted. Regal. Timeless.

Locs are a commitment and a crown. Sisterlocks start small and stay neat. Traditional locs get fuller and more dramatic over time. Both carry a quiet authority that commands any room.

Maintenance
CommitmentLong-term — not a try-before-you-buy
Best forBuilt for longevity — grows with you
Black women who own this Lisa Bonet, Alicia Keys, Lauryn Hill
On you: Sisterlocks would be stunning — fine locs that stay polished but get long fast. This is your "I have arrived" consulting brand energy, no explanation needed.

Look 06

Body Wave

Feminine. Flowing. Camera-Ready.

Big S-curve waves with volume and movement. The "I woke up like this" lie that takes two hours but convinces everyone you were born this way. Versatile, soft, and always ready.

Maintenance
Achievable viaSew-in, wig, or blowout + roller set
Best forBrand content, events, everyday glam
Black women who own this Gabrielle Union, Taraji P. Henson, Tracee Ellis Ross
On you: This is your content-day hair. It frames a round face beautifully and photographs with movement. Shoulder-to-mid-back length is the sweet spot for your frame.

All six styles above are well-suited to an oval/round face with high cheekbones and deep brown skin.
